In 1860 Samuel Wintrode, Christine’s third-great-grandfather, was farming in this neighbourhood,
post office Green Mount; the ridge very probably takes its name from the family.
Two doors off was Jacob Beamer, whose farm adjoined the Currens and Bushman lands,
and next to him Alexander Currens, whose house and barn were burned in the battle (Adams Sentinel, 14 July 1863) .
Samuel filed a claim for his own losses, and his son Edward served in the Adams County Cavalry,
